# Nepotism - Wikipedia

> ## Excerpt
> Nepotism is the act of granting an advantage, privilege, or position to relatives in an occupation or field. These fields can include retail, business, finance and  accounting as well as politics,  journalism, law, academia, entertainment, sports, religion, health care  and social work. In concept, it is similar to cronyism.[1][2]

---
[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Benjamin_Harrison_Astley_Cooper.jpg)

[Benjamin Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Harrison_(hospital_administrator) "Benjamin Harrison (hospital administrator)"), treasurer of [Guy's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy's_Hospital "Guy's Hospital") in London, was shown as a dominant presiding figure, with the nepotism of [Sir Astley Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astley_Cooper "Astley Cooper") having his tacit approval.

**Nepotism** is the act of granting an [advantage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-group_favoritism "In-group favoritism"), [privilege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_privilege "Social privilege"), or position to [relatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinship "Kinship") in an occupation or field. These fields can include retail, business, finance and [accounting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accounting "Accounting") as well as politics, [journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalism "Journalism"), [law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawyer "Lawyer"), academia, entertainment, sports, religion, [health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care "Health care") and [social work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_work "Social work"). In concept, it is similar to [cronyism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cronyism "Cronyism").<sup about="#mwt11" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-1&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-1" id="mwGQ"><span id="mwGg"><span id="mwGw">[</span>1<span id="mwHA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt14" id="cite_ref-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-2&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-2" id="mwHQ"><span id="mwHg"><span id="mwHw">[</span>2<span id="mwIA">]</span></span></a></sup>

The term originated with the [assignment of nephews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal-nephew "Cardinal-nephew"), sons, or other relatives to important positions by Catholic popes and bishops.<sup about="#mwt17" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-3&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-3" id="mwIw"><span id="mwJA"><span id="mwJQ">[</span>3<span id="mwJg">]</span></span></a></sup> Nepotism has been criticized since [ancient history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_history "Ancient history") by philosophers, including [Aristotle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristotle "Aristotle"), [Valluvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvalluvar "Thiruvalluvar"), and [Confucius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confucius "Confucius"), condemning it as both evil and unwise.<sup about="#mwt20" id="cite_ref-PSSundaram_Kural_4-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;PSSundaram_Kural&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-PSSundaram_Kural-4&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-PSSundaram_Kural-4" id="mwKw"><span id="mwLA"><span id="mwLQ">[</span>4<span id="mwLg">]</span></span></a></sup>

The term comes from the Italian word _nepotismo_,<sup about="#mwt24" id="cite_ref-dictionary_5-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;dictionary&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-dictionary-5&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-dictionary-5" id="mwNQ"><span id="mwNg"><span id="mwNw">[</span>5<span id="mwOA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt27" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-6" id="mwOQ"><span id="mwOg"><span id="mwOw">[</span>6<span id="mwPA">]</span></span></a></sup> which is based on the Latin root _nepos_ meaning nephew.<sup about="#mwt30" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-7&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-7" id="mwPg"><span id="mwPw"><span id="mwQA">[</span>7<span id="mwQQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Since the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages") and until the late 17th century, some [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism "Catholicism") popes and bishops – who had taken vows of [celibacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celibacy#Christianity "Celibacy") and, therefore, usually had no legitimate offspring of their own – gave their nephews such positions of preference as were often accorded by fathers to sons.<sup about="#mwt33" id="cite_ref-Article_Nepotism_8-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Article Nepotism&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Article_Nepotism-8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Article_Nepotism-8" id="mwRQ"><span id="mwRg"><span id="mwRw">[</span>8<span id="mwSA">]</span></span></a></sup> They would also do the same with children who were the illegitimate result of broken celibacy vows, and who were claimed to be "nephews" instead of sons.<sup about="#mwt36" id="cite_ref-Papal_Crimes_9-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Papal Crimes&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Papal_Crimes-9&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Papal_Crimes-9" id="mwSQ"><span id="mwSg"><span id="mwSw">[</span>9<span id="mwTA">]</span></span></a></sup>

Several popes [elevated nephews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal-nephew "Cardinal-nephew") and other relatives to the [cardinalate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholicism) "Cardinal (Catholicism)"). Often, such appointments were a means of continuing a papal "dynasty".<sup about="#mwt39" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-10&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-10" id="mwUA"><span id="mwUQ"><span id="mwUg">[</span>10<span id="mwUw">]</span></span></a></sup> For instance, [Pope Callixtus III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Callixtus_III "Pope Callixtus III"), head of the [Borgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Borgia "House of Borgia") family, made two of his nephews cardinals; one of them, Rodrigo, later used his position as a cardinal as a stepping stone to the papacy, becoming [Pope Alexander VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Alexander_VI "Pope Alexander VI").<sup about="#mwt42" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-11&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-11" id="mwVw"><span id="mwWA"><span id="mwWQ">[</span>11<span id="mwWg">]</span></span></a></sup> Alexander then elevated Alessandro Farnese, his mistress's brother, to cardinal; Farnese would later go on to become [Pope Paul III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_III "Pope Paul III").<sup about="#mwt45" id="cite_ref-12" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-12&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-12" id="mwXA"><span id="mwXQ"><span id="mwXg">[</span>12<span id="mwXw">]</span></span></a></sup> Paul III also engaged in nepotism, appointing, for instance, two illegitimate grandsons, aged 14 and 16, as cardinals. The practice was finally limited when [Pope Innocent XII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Innocent_XII "Pope Innocent XII") issued the [bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_bull "Papal bull") _[Romanum decet Pontificem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanum_decet_Pontificem "Romanum decet Pontificem")_ in 1692.<sup about="#mwt46" id="cite_ref-Article_Nepotism_8-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Article Nepotism&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Article_Nepotism-8" id="mwZA"><span id="mwZQ"><span id="mwZg">[</span>8<span id="mwZw">]</span></span></a></sup> The papal bull prohibited popes in all times from bestowing estates, offices, or revenues on any relative, with the exception that one qualified relative (at most) could be made a cardinal.<sup about="#mwt49" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-13&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-13" id="mwaA"><span id="mwaQ"><span id="mwag">[</span>13<span id="mwaw">]</span></span></a></sup>

### Mention in ancient literature

[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nepotism&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mention in ancient literature")

In the [second book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Porul "Book of Porul") of the [Kural literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirukkural "Tirukkural") from over 1,000 years ago, which formed a manual for governments and corporations in what is now India, philosopher [Valluvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valluvar "Valluvar") condemned favoritism as both evil and unwise:<sup about="#mwt50" id="cite_ref-PSSundaram_Kural_4-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;PSSundaram_Kural&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-PSSundaram_Kural-4" id="mwcQ"><span id="mwcg"><span id="mwcw">[</span>4<span id="mwdA">]</span></span></a></sup>

> If you choose an unfit person for your job just because you love and you like him, he will lead you to endless follies.<sup about="#mwt53" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-14&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-14" id="mwdw"><span id="mweA"><span id="mweQ">[</span>14<span id="mweg">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism is a common accusation in politics when the relative of a powerful figure ascends to similar power seemingly without appropriate qualifications. The [British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English "British English") expression "[Bob's your uncle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob's_your_uncle "Bob's your uncle")" is thought to have originated when [Robert Arthur Talbot Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Arthur_Talbot_Gascoyne-Cecil,_3rd_Marquess_of_Salisbury "Robert Arthur Talbot Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury"), promoted his nephew, [Arthur Balfour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Balfour "Arthur Balfour"), to the esteemed post of [Chief Secretary for Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Secretary_for_Ireland "Chief Secretary for Ireland"), which was widely seen as an act of nepotism.<sup about="#mwt54" id="cite_ref-Trahair_15-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Trahair&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Trahair-15&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Trahair-15" id="mwgw"><span id="mwhA"><span id="mwhQ">[</span>15<span id="mwhg">]</span></span></a></sup>

[Inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inheritance "Inheritance") has been viewed by some<sup about="#mwt55" id="mwiw"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch"><span title="The material near this tag possibly uses too-vague attribution or weasel words. (June 2026)">who?</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> as a form of nepotism.<sup about="#mwt58" id="cite_ref-e543_16-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;e543&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-e543-16&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-e543-16" id="mwjA"><span id="mwjQ"><span id="mwjg">[</span>16<span id="mwjw">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism in organizations leads to [monopolization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monopolization "Monopolization") of power because when members involved in institutional [decision-making](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision-making "Decision-making") are related, decisions made within institutions risk favoring a group of closely connected people.<sup about="#mwt61" id="cite_ref-17" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-17&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-17" id="mwlA"><span id="mwlQ"><span id="mwlg">[</span>17<span id="mwlw">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism can also occur within organizations, when a person is employed due to their familial ties.<sup about="#mwt64" id="cite_ref-18" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-18&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-18" id="mwmQ"><span id="mwmg"><span id="mwmw">[</span>18<span id="mwnA">]</span></span></a></sup> It is generally seen as unethical, both on the part of the employer and employee.<sup about="#mwt66" id="cite_ref-19" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-19&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-19" id="mwnQ"><span id="mwng"><span id="mwnw">[</span>19<span id="mwoA">]</span></span></a></sup> One of the consequences of nepotism in an organization is the creation of a limitation in the organization's network of contacts, reducing the opportunities for negotiation with other social circles, which can lead to a reduction in the success and duration of organizations in the long term.<sup about="#mwt71" id="cite_ref-20" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-20&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-20" id="mwoQ"><span id="mwog"><span id="mwow">[</span>20<span id="mwpA">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism at work can mean increased opportunity at a job, attaining a job or being paid more than other similarly situated people.<sup about="#mwt74" id="cite_ref-21" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-21&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-21" id="mwpw"><span id="mwqA"><span id="mwqQ">[</span>21<span id="mwqg">]</span></span></a></sup> Arguments are made both for and against employment granted due to a family connection, which is most common in small, [family-run businesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_business "Family business"). On one hand, nepotism can provide stability and continuity. Critics cite studies that demonstrate decreased morale and commitment from non-related employees,<sup about="#mwt77" id="cite_ref-22" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-22&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-22" id="mwrA"><span id="mwrQ"><span id="mwrg">[</span>22<span id="mwrw">]</span></span></a></sup> and a generally negative attitude towards superior positions filled through nepotism. A 2026 survey conducted by Kickresume of more than 1,000 respondents found that 61% of workers said they would have greater trust in their managers if promotions were based entirely on merit.<sup about="#mwt80" id="cite_ref-23" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-23&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-23" id="mwsA"><span id="mwsQ"><span id="mwsg">[</span>23<span id="mwsw">]</span></span></a></sup> An article from _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_ magazine stated, "there is no ladder to climb when the top rung is reserved for people with a certain name."<sup about="#mwt83" id="cite_ref-24" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-24&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-24" id="mwtg"><span id="mwtw"><span id="mwuA">[</span>24<span id="mwuQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Employing intimate people favors perpetuating the ideas or goals of those who employ them, knowing that the people around them will hold them. However, it can lead to a lack of competent staff or a reduction in [productivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productivity "Productivity") because even if the employees are not the best options for their functions, they will be protected by those who employ them.<sup about="#mwt86" id="cite_ref-25" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-25&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-25" id="mwuw"><span id="mwvA"><span id="mwvQ">[</span>25<span id="mwvg">]</span></span></a></sup>

Outside of national politics, accusations of "nepotism" are made in instances of _prima facie_ favoritism to relatives.

-   [Peaches Geldof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peaches_Geldof "Peaches Geldof")'s role as magazine editor in an [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") reality show – produced by a company owned by her father [Bob Geldof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Geldof "Bob Geldof")<sup about="#mwt89" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-26&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-26" id="mwyA"><span id="mwyQ"><span id="mwyg">[</span>26<span id="mwyw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt92" id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-27&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-27" id="mwzA"><span id="mwzQ"><span id="mwzg">[</span>27<span id="mwzw">]</span></span></a></sup>
-   [Tori Spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tori_Spelling "Tori Spelling") being cast on the TV series _[Beverly Hills, 90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_90210 "Beverly Hills, 90210")_ as a result of her father, [Aaron Spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Spelling "Aaron Spelling")'s, involvement with the show.<sup about="#mwt95" id="cite_ref-28" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-28&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-28" id="mw1Q"><span id="mw1g"><span id="mw1w">[</span>28<span id="mw2A">]</span></span></a></sup>
-   Hollywood's [Coppola family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppola_family_tree "Coppola family tree") includes many distinguished filmmakers and actors. The careers of [Sofia Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sofia_Coppola "Sofia Coppola"), [Nicolas Cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Cage "Nicolas Cage"), and [Jason Schwartzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Schwartzman "Jason Schwartzman") have been attributed to the aid of director [Francis Ford Coppola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Ford_Coppola "Francis Ford Coppola") who are Francis's daughter and nephews, respectively. He cast his daughter Sofia in _[The Godfather Part III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Godfather_Part_III "The Godfather Part III")_.<sup about="#mwt98" id="cite_ref-29" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-29&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-29" id="mw4Q"><span id="mw4g"><span id="mw4w">[</span>29<span id="mw5A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt101" id="cite_ref-30" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-30&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-30" id="mw5Q"><span id="mw5g"><span id="mw5w">[</span>30<span id="mw6A">]</span></span></a></sup> Cage changed his last name from Coppola to distance himself from his family professionally and minimize charges of favoritism.<sup about="#mwt104" id="cite_ref-31" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-31&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-31" id="mw6Q"><span id="mw6g"><span id="mw6w">[</span>31<span id="mw7A">]</span></span></a></sup>
-   [Ben Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Platt "Ben Platt")'s role as high schooler [Evan Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Hansen "Evan Hansen") in the [2021 film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dear_Evan_Hansen_(film) "Dear Evan Hansen (film)") of the musical _[Dear Evan Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dear_Evan_Hansen "Dear Evan Hansen")_ as a result of his winning the [Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical") for originating the role on Broadway in 2016, as well as the involvement of his father, [Marc Platt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Platt_(producer) "Marc Platt (producer)"), as one of the film's producers. The latter was never involved in the producing team of the stage version. The casting sparked controversy due to Ben Platt being ten years older than his character at the time of filming, resulting in critics and viewers deeming him too old to reprise his role.<sup about="#mwt107" id="cite_ref-32" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-32&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-32" id="mw9Q"><span id="mw9g"><span id="mw9w">[</span>32<span id="mw-A">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt110" id="cite_ref-33" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-33&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-33" id="mw-Q"><span id="mw-g"><span id="mw-w">[</span>33<span id="mw_A">]</span></span></a></sup> He would go on to be nominated for two [Golden Raspberry Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Awards "Golden Raspberry Awards"), including [Worst Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Raspberry_Award_for_Worst_Actor "Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Actor"), for his performance.<sup about="#mwt113" id="cite_ref-34" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-34&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-34" id="mw_w"><span id="mwAQA"><span id="mwAQE">[</span>34<span id="mwAQI">]</span></span></a></sup>
-   [_New York_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(magazine) "New York (magazine)") magazine's December 2022 cover (calling 2022 'The Year of the [Nepo Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepo_baby "Nepo baby")') featured notable celebrities ([Maude Apatow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maude_Apatow "Maude Apatow"), [Lily-Rose Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily-Rose_Depp "Lily-Rose Depp"), [Maya Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_Hawke "Maya Hawke"), [Dakota Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakota_Johnson "Dakota Johnson"), Ben Platt, [Jack Quaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Quaid "Jack Quaid"), [Zoë Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%AB_Kravitz "Zoë Kravitz"), and [John David Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_David_Washington "John David Washington")) whose career successes have been achieved through nepotism.<sup about="#mwt116" id="cite_ref-35" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-35&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-35" id="mwAQ4"><span id="mwAQ8"><span id="mwARA">[</span>35<span id="mwARE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt119" id="cite_ref-36" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-36&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-36" id="mwARI"><span id="mwARM"><span id="mwARQ">[</span>36<span id="mwARU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt122" id="cite_ref-37" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-37&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-37" id="mwARY"><span id="mwARc"><span id="mwARg">[</span>37<span id="mwARk">]</span></span></a></sup>

-   [Thanasis Antetokounmpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanasis_Antetokounmpo "Thanasis Antetokounmpo") has been labeled the beneficiary of nepotism due to his brother being [Giannis Antetokounmpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giannis_Antetokounmpo "Giannis Antetokounmpo"), even though his play is deemed by some to not be good enough for him to occupy a roster spot on the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks").<sup about="#mwt125" id="cite_ref-38" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-38&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-38" id="mwASA"><span id="mwASE"><span id="mwASI">[</span>38<span id="mwASM">]</span></span></a></sup>
-   The [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") encountered allegations of nepotism when they selected [Bronny James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronny_James "Bronny James"), the son of [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), in the [2024 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft "2024 NBA draft"). Although other NBA prospects exemplified greater promise, experts questioned Bronny's NBA readiness due to his lackluster performance during his only NCAA season. Reports revealed that LeBron's agent, [Rich Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Paul "Rich Paul"), actively discouraged other teams from drafting Bronny, even going so far as to suggest that he might play overseas if selected.<sup about="#mwt128" id="cite_ref-39" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-39&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-39" id="mwASo"><span id="mwASs"><span id="mwASw">[</span>39<span id="mwAS0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt131" id="cite_ref-40" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-40&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-40" id="mwAS4"><span id="mwAS8"><span id="mwATA">[</span>40<span id="mwATE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt134" id="cite_ref-41" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-41&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-41" id="mwATI"><span id="mwATM"><span id="mwATQ">[</span>41<span id="mwATU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt137" id="cite_ref-42" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-42&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-42" id="mwATY"><span id="mwATc"><span id="mwATg">[</span>42<span id="mwATk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt140" id="cite_ref-43" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-43&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-43" id="mwATo"><span id="mwATs"><span id="mwATw">[</span>43<span id="mwAT0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt143" id="cite_ref-44" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-44&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-44" id="mwAT4"><span id="mwAT8"><span id="mwAUA">[</span>44<span id="mwAUE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt146" id="cite_ref-45" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-45&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-45" id="mwAUI"><span id="mwAUM"><span id="mwAUQ">[</span>45<span id="mwAUU">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism is found in academia, where it is common for professors to have their partners, and sometimes children, hired by the same faculty in which they work.<sup about="#mwt151" id="cite_ref-46" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-46&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-46" id="mwAUo"><span id="mwAUs"><span id="mwAUw">[</span>46<span id="mwAU0">]</span></span></a></sup> In the second half of the 20th century, in the United States at least, this was far less frequent as universities typically held very strict anti-nepotism policies.<sup about="#mwt154" id="cite_ref-47" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-47&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-47" id="mwAU4"><span id="mwAU8"><span id="mwAVA">[</span>47<span id="mwAVE">]</span></span></a></sup> Countries with high levels of corruption and higher education systems with low competition between universities generally have higher levels of corruption in academia.<sup about="#mwt157" id="cite_ref-48" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-48&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-48" id="mwAVI"><span id="mwAVM"><span id="mwAVQ">[</span>48<span id="mwAVU">]</span></span></a></sup> Italy has been noted for having particularly high levels of nepotism in its academic system, when compared to other developed nations.<sup about="#mwt160" id="cite_ref-49" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-49&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-49" id="mwAVY"><span id="mwAVc"><span id="mwAVg">[</span>49<span id="mwAVk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt163" id="cite_ref-50" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-50&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-50" id="mwAVo"><span id="mwAVs"><span id="mwAVw">[</span>50<span id="mwAV0">]</span></span></a></sup> Nepotism is often praised for favoring female employment in academia.<sup about="#mwt166" id="cite_ref-51" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-51&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-51" id="mwAV4"><span id="mwAV8"><span id="mwAWA">[</span>51<span id="mwAWE">]</span></span></a></sup>

## Selected examples by country

[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nepotism&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Selected examples by country")

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Opening_of_the_Crimean_bridge_(2018-05-15)_01.jpg)

[Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin")'s childhood friend [Arkady Rotenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkady_Rotenberg "Arkady Rotenberg") is one of the richest people in Russia.<sup about="#mwt169" id="cite_ref-52" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-52&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-52" id="mwAWk"><span id="mwAWo"><span id="mwAWs">[</span>52<span id="mwAWw">]</span></span></a></sup>

In [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), nepotism is a common practice. Although there have been various attempts at reducing it,<sup about="#mwt173" id="cite_ref-53" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-53&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-53" id="mwAXA"><span id="mwAXE"><span id="mwAXI">[</span>53<span id="mwAXM">]</span></span></a></sup> it is difficult in a country where state jobs are used as a token of gratitude or party favoritism.<sup about="#mwt170" id="mwAXU"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2025)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

Former president [Mauricio Macri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauricio_Macri "Mauricio Macri") has been investigated for nepotism after allegedly extending a tax amnesty to his family.<sup about="#mwt176" id="cite_ref-54" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-54&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-54" id="mwAXg"><span id="mwAXk"><span id="mwAXo">[</span>54<span id="mwAXs">]</span></span></a></sup> Nonetheless, in 2018, the government of Mauricio Macri set a limit on nepotism through Decree 93/2018<sup about="#mwt179" id="cite_ref-55" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-55&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-55" id="mwAXw"><span id="mwAX0"><span id="mwAX4">[</span>55<span id="mwAX8">]</span></span></a></sup> establishing that "appointments of people could no longer be made, under any modality, throughout the National Public Sector, who have some kinship link both in straight line as well as in a collateral line up to the second degree, with the President and Vice President of the Nation, Chief of the Cabinet of Ministers, Ministers and other officials with the rank and hierarchy of Minister. The spouse and the Cohabitant Union are included. "

The [Kirchnerist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirchnerist "Kirchnerist") movement has been openly accused of believing in nepotism, treating meritocracy as a pejorative concept.<sup about="#mwt182" id="cite_ref-56" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-56&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-56" id="mwAYI"><span id="mwAYM"><span id="mwAYQ">[</span>56<span id="mwAYU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt185" id="cite_ref-57" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-57&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-57" id="mwAYY"><span id="mwAYc"><span id="mwAYg">[</span>57<span id="mwAYk">]</span></span></a></sup> The government's ministries and secretariats are reportedly plagued with friends, family and supporters of the current party leaders, many of whom have been criticized for being incompetent at their jobs.<sup about="#mwt188" id="cite_ref-58" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-58&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-58" id="mwAYo"><span id="mwAYs"><span id="mwAYw">[</span>58<span id="mwAY0">]</span></span></a></sup>

On December 10, 2023, the libertarian president [Javier Milei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Milei "Javier Milei") takes office – who campaigned criticizing the political "caste", an entelechy built to denigrate traditional political parties and among whose characteristics is that of appointing friends and family to public positions on a discretionary basis – and in one of his first measures he modifies the Mauricio Macri's Decree 93/2018 to be able to grant his sister, [Karina Milei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karina_Milei "Karina Milei"), the position of General Secretary of the Presidency.<sup about="#mwt191" id="cite_ref-59" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-59&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-59" id="mwAZE"><span id="mwAZI"><span id="mwAZM">[</span>59<span id="mwAZQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Less than two months later, Francisco Adorni, the brother of the government spokesperson [Manuel Adorni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Adorni "Manuel Adorni"), took a position as an advisor in the Ministry of Defense.<sup about="#mwt194" id="cite_ref-60" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-60&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-60" id="mwAZY"><span id="mwAZc"><span id="mwAZg">[</span>60<span id="mwAZk">]</span></span></a></sup>

Shortly after he was appointed the Anglican Archbishop of Sydney in 2001, [Peter Jensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Jensen_(bishop) "Peter Jensen (bishop)") was accused, in an Australian Broadcasting Corporation interview, of nepotism after nominating his brother [Phillip Jensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillip_Jensen "Phillip Jensen") as Dean of Sydney and appointing his wife Christine Jensen to an official position in the Sydney diocese.<sup about="#mwt197" id="cite_ref-61" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-61&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-61" id="mwAZ4"><span id="mwAZ8"><span id="mwAaA">[</span>61<span id="mwAaE">]</span></span></a></sup>

[Anna Bligh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Bligh "Anna Bligh"), who won the 2009 Queensland State election, has been accused of nepotism for giving her husband, Greg Withers, a position as the Office of Climate Change head.<sup about="#mwt200" id="cite_ref-houghton_62-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;houghton&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-houghton-62&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-houghton-62" id="mwAaQ"><span id="mwAaU"><span id="mwAaY">[</span>62<span id="mwAac">]</span></span></a></sup>

[Football Federation Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Federation_Australia "Football Federation Australia") was led by [Frank Lowy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lowy "Frank Lowy") from its inception in 2004 until his [term limit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Term_limit "Term limit") exit in 2015. His son, [Steven Lowy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Lowy "Steven Lowy"), who had little direct involvement in high-level sports governance, was nominated as his replacement by Frank, and was elected unopposed by a board strongly loyal to Frank. Steven's introduction exacerbated existing governance issues, with factional opposition led by [City Football Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Football_Group "City Football Group") causing [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") intervention to be threatened. Eventually, governance reforms were forced through despite opposition from the Lowy family, and it ended with Steven Lowy resigning from the role. Lowy had also been accused of nepotism regarding his sons in his corporate dealings as the founder of [Westfield Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westfield_Group "Westfield Group").<sup about="#mwt203" id="cite_ref-63" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-63&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-63" id="mwAbA"><span id="mwAbE"><span id="mwAbI">[</span>63<span id="mwAbM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt206" id="cite_ref-64" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-64&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-64" id="mwAbQ"><span id="mwAbU"><span id="mwAbY">[</span>64<span id="mwAbc">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ilham_Aliyev_paid_tribute_to_Azerbaijani_martyrs_7.jpg)

Aliyev family in 2018

On 21 February 2017, [President of Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Azerbaijan "President of Azerbaijan") [Ilham Aliyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilham_Aliyev "Ilham Aliyev") created the position of [Vice President of Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_Azerbaijan "Vice President of Azerbaijan"), then appointed his wife, [Mehriban Aliyeva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehriban_Aliyeva "Mehriban Aliyeva"), to the position.<sup about="#mwt209" id="cite_ref-65" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-65&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-65" id="mwAcI"><span id="mwAcM"><span id="mwAcQ">[</span>65<span id="mwAcU">]</span></span></a></sup> Since 1993, the presidency of Azerbaijan has always been in the hands of a member of the Aliyev family: in 1993, [Heydar Aliyev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heydar_Aliyev "Heydar Aliyev") was elected president of Azerbaijan, and after his death in a United States hospital in 2003, his son Ilham Aliyev became president and has been since then. His regime has been accused of a lack of democratic freedoms and press freedom.<sup about="#mwt212" id="cite_ref-66" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-66&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-66" id="mwAcc"><span id="mwAcg"><span id="mwAck">[</span>66<span id="mwAco">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt215" id="cite_ref-67" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-67&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-67" id="mwAcs"><span id="mwAcw"><span id="mwAc0">[</span>67<span id="mwAc4">]</span></span></a></sup>

Over the past decade, criticism has been growing over the creation of political dynasties in Belgium. This phenomenon has been explained by the fact that prominent party members control the ranking of candidates on party lists for elections and a candidate's place on a list determines who is elected. Another justification for the phenomenon is the importance of name recognition for collecting votes.<sup about="#mwt218" id="cite_ref-autogenerated1_68-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;autogenerated1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-autogenerated1-68&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-autogenerated1-68" id="mwAdE"><span id="mwAdI"><span id="mwAdM">[</span>68<span id="mwAdQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

Claims of nepotism have been made against [Bruno Tobback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Tobback "Bruno Tobback"), the son of senator and former minister [Louis Tobback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Tobback "Louis Tobback"), a member of the Flemish socialists. He became the Belgian federal government's minister for pensions and environment at 35 in 2005.<sup about="#mwt221" id="cite_ref-69" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-69&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-69" id="mwAdg"><span id="mwAdk"><span id="mwAdo">[</span>69<span id="mwAds">]</span></span></a></sup> [Alexander De Croo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_De_Croo "Alexander De Croo"), the son of former speaker of the Belgian parliament Herman De Croo, ran for the leadership of his father's party Open VLD at age 33.<sup about="#mwt224" id="cite_ref-70" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-70&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-70" id="mwAd0"><span id="mwAd4"><span id="mwAd8">[</span>70<span id="mwAeA">]</span></span></a></sup> Finally, there is the example of [Maya Detiège](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_Deti%C3%A8ge "Maya Detiège"), the daughter of former mayor of the city of [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") Leona Detiège, who herself is the daughter of the former mayor of [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") Frans Detiège.<sup about="#mwt225" id="cite_ref-autogenerated1_68-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;autogenerated1&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-autogenerated1-68" id="mwAeQ"><span id="mwAeU"><span id="mwAeY">[</span>68<span id="mwAec">]</span></span></a></sup> Among other examples are former minister [Freya Van Den Bossche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freya_Van_den_Bossche "Freya Van den Bossche") and senator [Jean-Jacques De Gucht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Jacques_De_Gucht "Jean-Jacques De Gucht"), being the daughter and son, respectively, of former minister [Luc Vandenbossche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luc_Van_den_Bossche "Luc Van den Bossche") and former minister [Karel De Gucht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karel_De_Gucht "Karel De Gucht").

[Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Cambodia "Prime Minister of Cambodia") [Hun Sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hun_Sen "Hun Sen") and senior members of [Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Cambodia "Parliament of Cambodia") are known for their hand in getting family members into government positions. In the [2013 Cambodian parliamentary elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Cambodian_general_election "2013 Cambodian general election"), at least eight candidates were sons of high-ranking [Cambodian People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodian_People's_Party "Cambodian People's Party") officials.<sup about="#mwt228" id="cite_ref-71" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-71&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-71" id="mwAfM"><span id="mwAfQ"><span id="mwAfU">[</span>71<span id="mwAfY">]</span></span></a></sup> All sons of the ruling party lost but were eventually appointed to high-ranking government positions.

For the past 3,000 years, nepotism has been common in China's clan and extended family-based culture. [Confucius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confucius "Confucius") wrote about the importance of balancing "filial piety with merit". The [clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan "Clan")\-based [feudal system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feudal_society "Feudal society") collapsed during Confucius' lifetime, yet nepotism has continued through the modern age.<sup about="#mwt233" id="cite_ref-72" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-72&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-72" id="mwAf4"><span id="mwAf8"><span id="mwAgA">[</span>72<span id="mwAgE">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt236" id="cite_ref-73" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-73&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-73" id="mwAgI"><span id="mwAgM"><span id="mwAgQ">[</span>73<span id="mwAgU">]</span></span></a></sup>

In October 2009, [Jean Sarkozy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Sarkozy "Jean Sarkozy"), the second son of the [President of the French Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_France "President of France"), [Nicolas Sarkozy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Sarkozy "Nicolas Sarkozy"), was poised to become the director of the major [EPAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tablissement_public_pour_l'am%C3%A9nagement_de_la_r%C3%A9gion_de_la_D%C3%A9fense?action=edit&redlink=1 "Établissement public pour l'aménagement de la région de la Défense (page does not exist)") \[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89tablissement%20public%20pour%20l'am%C3%A9nagement%20de%20la%20r%C3%A9gion%20de%20la%20D%C3%A9fense "fr:Établissement public pour l'aménagement de la région de la Défense")\] authority despite lacking any higher education degree and professional experience.<sup about="#mwt240" id="cite_ref-74" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-74&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-74" id="mwAg0"><span id="mwAg4"><span id="mwAg8">[</span>74<span id="mwAhA">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2008, he was voted general councillor of [Neuilly-sur-Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuilly-sur-Seine "Neuilly-sur-Seine"), the town of which his father had previously been mayor.<sup about="#mwt243" id="cite_ref-75" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-75&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-75" id="mwAhI"><span id="mwAhM"><span id="mwAhQ">[</span>75<span id="mwAhU">]</span></span></a></sup>

In September 2009, [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping")\-producer Pierre Sarkozy, the first son of then-President Nicolas Sarkozy, asked [SCPP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCPP?action=edit&redlink=1 "SCPP (page does not exist)") <sup about="#mwt244" id="mwAhk"><span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><a rel="mw:WikiLink/Interwiki" href="https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9%20civile%20des%20producteurs%20phonographiques" title="fr:Société civile des producteurs phonographiques">fr</a><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> for a financial contribution of around €10000 towards an €80000 artistic project. Because he was not an SCPP member, the request was automatically rejected. Pierre Sarkozy then went to the [Élysée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89lys%C3%A9e "Élysée"), which led to an Élysée aide contacting the SCPP, and SCPP president Marc Guez assuring the issue would soon be favorably resolved.<sup about="#mwt248" id="cite_ref-76" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-76&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-76" id="mwAhs"><span id="mwAhw"><span id="mwAh0">[</span>76<span id="mwAh4">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt251" id="cite_ref-77" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-77&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-77" id="mwAh8"><span id="mwAiA"><span id="mwAiE">[</span>77<span id="mwAiI">]</span></span></a></sup> According to [Abeille Musique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abeille_Musique?action=edit&redlink=1 "Abeille Musique (page does not exist)") <sup about="#mwt245" id="mwAiQ"><span typeof="mw:Entity">&nbsp;</span><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><a rel="mw:WikiLink/Interwiki" href="https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abeille%20Musique" title="fr:Abeille Musique">fr</a><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> president and SCPP member Yves Riesel, however, this would not happen as SCPP's financial help has been restricted to members only for months.<sup about="#mwt254" id="cite_ref-78" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-78&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-78" id="mwAiU"><span id="mwAiY"><span id="mwAic">[</span>78<span id="mwAig">]</span></span></a></sup>

In Greece, it is common practice for family members of current or former party leaders to be party members and get appointed as ministers when the party is in government.<sup about="#mwt257" id="cite_ref-79" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-79&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-79" id="mwAis"><span id="mwAiw"><span id="mwAi0">[</span>79<span id="mwAi4">]</span></span></a></sup> In addition, there have been three prime ministers from the [Papandreou family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_political_families_in_Greece#P "List of political families in Greece"),<sup about="#mwt260" id="cite_ref-80" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-80&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-80" id="mwAjA"><span id="mwAjE"><span id="mwAjI">[</span>80<span id="mwAjM">]</span></span></a></sup> two from the [Mitsotakis family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_political_families_in_Greece#M "List of political families in Greece") (one currently serving),<sup about="#mwt263" id="cite_ref-81" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-81&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-81" id="mwAjU"><span id="mwAjY"><span id="mwAjc">[</span>81<span id="mwAjg">]</span></span></a></sup> two from the [Karamanlis family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_political_families_in_Greece#K "List of political families in Greece") (a third one was serving as minister of transportation until February 2023, quitting his position following the worst rail disaster in the history of the country).

Research conducted found that in India, family CEOs are generally paid more than professional CEOs, especially in high-performing, eponymous firms. Additionally, family CEOs in these firms exhibit greater pay-performance sensitivity, benefiting more from strong performance while remaining insulated from poor outcomes. These findings indicate that CEO compensation can be used by controlling families in emerging markets as a tool to extract private benefits, often at the expense of minority shareholders.<sup about="#mwt266" id="cite_ref-82" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-82&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-82" id="mwAjw"><span id="mwAj0"><span id="mwAj4">[</span>82<span id="mwAj8">]</span></span></a></sup>

#### Nepotism in Indian politics

[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nepotism&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Nepotism in Indian politics")

Since the 1980s, Indian politics has become dynastic, possibly due to the absence of elected party organization, independent civil society associations that mobilize support for a party, and centralized financing of elections.<sup about="#mwt274" id="cite_ref-83" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-83&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-83" id="mwAkQ"><span id="mwAkU"><span id="mwAkY">[</span>83<span id="mwAkc">]</span></span></a></sup> One example of dynastic politics has been the [Nehru–Gandhi family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nehru%E2%80%93Gandhi_family "Nehru–Gandhi family"), which produced [three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_prime_ministers_of_India "List of prime ministers of India") Indian prime ministers. Family members have also led the [Congress Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") for most of the period since 1978, when [Indira Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi "Indira Gandhi") floated the then Congress(I) faction of the party.<sup about="#mwt277" id="cite_ref-84" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-84&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-84" id="mwAkw"><span id="mwAk0"><span id="mwAk4">[</span>84<span id="mwAk8">]</span></span></a></sup> The ruling [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") also features several senior leaders who are dynasts.<sup about="#mwt280" id="cite_ref-85" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-85&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-85" id="mwAlE"><span id="mwAlI"><span id="mwAlM">[</span>85<span id="mwAlQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Dynastic politics is prevalent also in a number of political parties with regional presence such as [Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dravida_Munnetra_Kazhagam "Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam") (DMK), [Indian National Lok Dal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Lok_Dal "Indian National Lok Dal") (INLD), [Jammu & Kashmir National Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jammu_&_Kashmir_National_Conference "Jammu & Kashmir National Conference") (JKNC), [Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jammu_and_Kashmir_Peoples_Democratic_Party "Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party") (JKPDP), [All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_India_Majlis-e-Ittehadul_Muslimeen "All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen") (AIMIM), [Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desiya_Murpokku_Dravida_Kazhagam "Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam") (DMDK), [Janata Dal (Secular)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janata_Dal_(Secular) "Janata Dal (Secular)") (JD(s)), [Jannayak Janta Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jannayak_Janta_Party "Jannayak Janta Party") (JJP) [Jharkhand Mukti Morcha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jharkhand_Mukti_Morcha "Jharkhand Mukti Morcha") (JMM), [National People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_People's_Party_(India) "National People's Party (India)") (NPP), [Nationalist Congress Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_Congress_Party "Nationalist Congress Party") (NCP), [Pattali Makkal Many judges and advocates of the [high courts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_courts_of_India "High courts of India") and the [Supreme Court of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India "Supreme Court of India") are alleged to be appointed by exercising casteism, nepotism,<sup about="#mwt286" id="cite_ref-88" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-88&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-89" id="mwAnk"><span id="mwAno"><span id="mwAns">[</span>89<span id="mwAnw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt292" id="cite_ref-90" legally binding manner, the names of judges to be appointed or promoted to the higher judiciary. The various judicial services exams are also infamous for these practices.<sup about="#mwt298" id="cite_ref-92" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-92&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-92" id="mwAoY"><span id="mwAoc"><span id="mwAog">[</span>92<span id="mwAok">]</span></span></a></sup>
