[Suharto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suharto "Suharto"), Indonesia's second president, is involved in nepotism, alongside corruption and [collusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collusion "Collusion") (together, they are known as the _KKN_ in [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language "Indonesian language"): _korupsi, kolusi, dan nepotisme_). Companies belonging to Suharto's children, particularly Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana ("Tutut"), Hutomo Mandala Putra ("Tommy"), and Bambang Trihatmodjo, were given lucrative government contracts and protected from market competition by monopolies. Examples include the toll-expressway company [Jasamarga](https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasamarga "id:Jasamarga") (monopolized by Tutut), the national car project [Timor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timor "Timor") (monopolized by Bambang and Tommy), and the cinema market (monopolized by [21 Cineplex](https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/21%20Cineplex "id:21 Cineplex"), which is owned by Suharto's cousin Sudwikatmono). The family is said to control about 36,000 km<sup about="#mwt323">2</sup> (14,000 sq mi) of real estate in Indonesia, including 100,000 m<sup about="#mwt324">2</sup> (1,100,000 sq ft) of prime office space in Jakarta and nearly 40% of the land in [East Timor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Timor "East Timor"). Additionally, Suharto's family members received free shares in 1,251 of Indonesia's most lucrative domestic companies (mostly run by Suharto's ethnic-Chinese cronies), while foreign-owned companies were encouraged to establish "strategic partnerships" with the former Indonesian president's family companies.<sup about="#mwt327" id="cite_ref-BBC_20040325_100-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;BBC_20040325&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-BBC_20040325-100&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-BBC_20040325-100" id="mwAsw"><span id="mwAs0"><span id="mwAs4">[</span>100<span id="mwAs8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt330" id="cite_ref-Global_Corruption_Report_101-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Global Corruption Report&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Global_Corruption_Report-101&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Global_Corruption_Report-101" id="mwAtA"><span id="mwAtE"><span id="mwAtI">[</span>101<span id="mwAtM">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2024, Suharto's former son in law [Prabowo Subianto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabowo_Subianto "Prabowo Subianto") became President of Indonesia.<sup about="#mwt333" id="cite_ref-102" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-102&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-102" id="mwAtU"><span id="mwAtY"><span id="mwAtc">[</span>102<span id="mwAtg">]</span></span></a></sup>

Since the [first democratic elections in 1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Mauritian_general_election "1948 Mauritian general election"), the field of politics in Mauritius has been marked by a handful of families who have controlled the four major political parties which exist to this day. They are often referred to as the "modern dynasties" of Mauritian politics, such as the Duval, Bérenger, Gunowa (Gungah), Curé, Uteem, Mohamed, Boolell, Ramgoolam and Jugnauth families. The Boolell family's involvement in politics started with [Satcam Boolell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satcam_Boolell "Satcam Boolell") in 1955, paving the way for his son [Arvin Boolell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arvin_Boolell "Arvin Boolell"), nephews Satish Boolell, Anil Gayan, and Sanjay Bhuckory, and son-in-law Sushil Kushiram to enter politics. The Duval dynasty started with ex-[Lord mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_mayor "Lord mayor") and minister Gaetan Duval, followed by his sons Xavier and Richard, as well as his grandson Adrien. Lall Jugnauth was the first of his clan to enter politics in the 1950s and was followed by his cousins Aneerood and Ashock as well as his nephew Pravind. Abdool Razack Mohamed, who migrated from India in the 1930s, became Lord Mayor and minister; his son, Yousuf and grandson, Shakeel, were also elected and served as ministers.<sup about="#mwt338" id="cite_ref-103" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-103&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-103" id="mwAuE"><span id="mwAuI"><span id="mwAuM">[</span>103<span id="mwAuQ">]</span></span></a></sup> [Roshi Bhadain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roshi_Bhadain "Roshi Bhadain"), who was a minister of the [MSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Militant_Socialist_Movement "Militant Socialist Movement") government, is the nephew of former Labour Party minister [Vasant Bunwaree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasant_Bunwaree "Vasant Bunwaree").<sup about="#mwt341" id="cite_ref-104" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-104&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-104" id="mwAug"><span id="mwAuk"><span id="mwAuo">[</span>104<span id="mwAus">]</span></span></a></sup> [Roshi Bhadain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roshi_Bhadain "Roshi Bhadain") and Akilesh Deerpalsing (Bhadain's advisor and campaign manager, who is also the son of former minister [Kishore Deerpalsing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Deerpalsing "Kishore Deerpalsing")) were investigated by [ICAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Commission_Against_Corruption_(Mauritius) "Independent Commission Against Corruption (Mauritius)") in 2019 for suspicious recruitment practices when he was a minister.<sup about="#mwt344" id="cite_ref-105" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-105&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-105" id="mwAu8"><span id="mwAvA"><span id="mwAvE">[</span>105<span id="mwAvI">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt347" id="cite_ref-106" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-106&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-106" id="mwAvM"><span id="mwAvQ"><span id="mwAvU">[</span>106<span id="mwAvY">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt350" id="cite_ref-107" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-107&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-107" id="mwAvc"><span id="mwAvg"><span id="mwAvk">[</span>107<span id="mwAvo">]</span></span></a></sup>

In March 2020, Harry Ganoo, the retired brother of Minister [Alan Ganoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Ganoo "Alan Ganoo"), was nominated as the new president of the Civil Service College Mauritius, a few months after the November 2019 General Elections.<sup about="#mwt353" id="cite_ref-108" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-108&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-108" id="mwAv0"><span id="mwAv4"><span id="mwAv8">[</span>108<span id="mwAwA">]</span></span></a></sup>

The appointment of [Nurul Izzah Anwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nurul_Izzah_Anwar "Nurul Izzah Anwar") as a senior economic and finance advisor by Prime Minister [Anwar Ibrahim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anwar_Ibrahim "Anwar Ibrahim") resulted in accusations of nepotism.<sup about="#mwt356" id="cite_ref-109" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-109&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-109" id="mwAwU"><span id="mwAwY"><span id="mwAwc">[</span>109<span id="mwAwg">]</span></span></a></sup> The action was widely criticized by intellectuals, NGOs and even party members of the Pakatan Harapan coalition, who claimed it contravened principles of merit and fairness.<sup about="#mwt359" id="cite_ref-110" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-110&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-110" id="mwAwk"><span id="mwAwo"><span id="mwAws">[</span>110<span id="mwAww">]</span></span></a></sup>

Due to its small native population, Malta has an entrenched culture of nepotism, which became more evident since the country gained independence from the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") in 1964.<sup about="#mwt364" id="cite_ref-111" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-111&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-111" id="mwAxI"><span id="mwAxM"><span id="mwAxQ">[</span>111<span id="mwAxU">]</span></span></a></sup>

In a Eurobarometer survey published in 2023, 55% of Maltese businesses reported that nepotism and patronage were primary problems, and 70% said close links between businesspeople and politicians led to corruption.<sup about="#mwt367" id="cite_ref-:0_112-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:0&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:0-112&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-:0-112" id="mwAxc"><span id="mwAxg"><span id="mwAxk">[</span>112<span id="mwAxo">]</span></span></a></sup>

By comparison, only 37% of respondents in other EU member states saw nepotism and patronage as problematic, and 35% cited corruption as a concern.<sup about="#mwt368" id="cite_ref-:0_112-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:0&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-:0-112" id="mwAxw"><span id="mwAx0"><span id="mwAx4">[</span>112<span id="mwAx8">]</span></span></a></sup>

Members of the [Romanian Communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Romania "Socialist Republic of Romania") dictator [Nicolae Ceaușescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolae_Ceau%C8%99escu "Nicolae Ceaușescu")'s family dominated the country for decades.<sup about="#mwt371" id="cite_ref-113" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-113&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-113" id="mwAyQ"><span id="mwAyU"><span id="mwAyY">[</span>113<span id="mwAyc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt374" id="cite_ref-114" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-114&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-114" id="mwAyg"><span id="mwAyk"><span id="mwAyo">[</span>114<span id="mwAys">]</span></span></a></sup> [Elena Băsescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_B%C4%83sescu "Elena Băsescu"), the daughter of President [Traian Băsescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traian_B%C4%83sescu "Traian Băsescu"), was elected to the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") in 2009, despite having no significant professional or political experience.<sup about="#mwt377" id="cite_ref-115" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-115&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-115" id="mwAy8"><span id="mwAzA"><span id="mwAzE">[</span>115<span id="mwAzI">]</span></span></a></sup>

[Singapore's government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Singapore "Government of Singapore") has been the target of numerous charges of nepotism, with several members of the [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Singapore "Prime Minister of Singapore")'s family holding high-ranking posts. [Lee Kuan Yew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Kuan_Yew "Lee Kuan Yew"), who was prime minister from 1959 to 1990, preceded his son [Lee Hsien Loong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Hsien_Loong "Lee Hsien Loong"). Other family members holding high positions include the elder Lee's daughter, [Lee Wei Ling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Wei_Ling "Lee Wei Ling"), the director of the National Neurological Institute, his other son, [Lee Hsien Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Hsien_Yang "Lee Hsien Yang"), the chief executive officer of [Singapore Telecommunications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singtel "Singtel") from 1995 to 2007 and the younger Lee's wife, [Ho Ching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Ching "Ho Ching"), who was appointed [chief executive officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of state holding investment company [Temasek Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temasek_Holdings "Temasek Holdings"). The family members dispute the charges as they arise.<sup about="#mwt382" id="cite_ref-116" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-116&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-116" id="mwA0E"><span id="mwA0I"><span id="mwA0M">[</span>116<span id="mwA0Q">]</span></span></a></sup>

Former President of Sri Lanka, [Mahinda Rajapaksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahinda_Rajapaksa "Mahinda Rajapaksa"), has been accused of nepotism, appointing three brothers to run important ministries and giving out other political positions to relatives, regardless of their merit. During his presidency, the Rajapaksa family held the ministries of [finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Finance_and_Planning_(Sri_Lanka) "Ministry of Finance and Planning (Sri Lanka)"), [defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defence_minister "Defence minister"), [ports and aviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Ports_and_Aviation_(Sri_Lanka) "Ministry of Ports and Aviation (Sri Lanka)"), and [highways and road development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Highways_and_Road_Development_(Sri_Lanka) "Ministry of Highways and Road Development (Sri Lanka)"). The president's brother, [Gotabhaya Rajapaksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gotabhaya_Rajapaksa "Gotabhaya Rajapaksa"), was given the post of [Defence Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Sri_Lanka) "Ministry of Defence (Sri Lanka)"). He also controlled the armed forces, the police and the Coast Guard, and was responsible for immigration and emigration. Rajapaksa appointed his brother [Basil Rajapaksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basil_Rajapaksa "Basil Rajapaksa") as Minister of Economic Development. Together, the Rajapaksa brothers controlled over 70% of Sri Lanka's public budget. Mahinda Rajapaksa's eldest brother, [Chamal Rajapaksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamal_Rajapaksa "Chamal Rajapaksa"), was appointed as the [Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_Parliament_of_Sri_Lanka "Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka"), and has held many other posts before, while his eldest son, Namal Rajapaksa, is also a member of the parliament and holds undisclosed portfolios.<sup about="#mwt387" id="cite_ref-117" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-117&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-117" id="mwA1M"><span id="mwA1Q"><span id="mwA1U">[</span>117<span id="mwA1Y">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt390" id="cite_ref-atimes1_118-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;atimes1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-atimes1-118&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-atimes1-118" id="mwA1c"><span id="mwA1g"><span id="mwA1k">[</span>118<span id="mwA1o">]</span></span></a></sup>

Others include his nephew, [Shashindra Rajapaksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashindra_Rajapaksa "Shashindra Rajapaksa"), the former [Chief Minister of Uva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Uva "Chief Minister of Uva"); one of his cousins, [Jaliya Wickramasuriya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaliya_Wickramasuriya "Jaliya Wickramasuriya"), the former Sri Lankan ambassador to the United States; and another cousin, [Udayanga Weeratunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udayanga_Weeratunga "Udayanga Weeratunga"), the former ambassador to Russia. Dozens of nephews, nieces, cousins, and in-laws have also been appointed heads of banks, boards, and corporations.<sup about="#mwt391" id="cite_ref-atimes1_118-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;atimes1&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-atimes1-118" id="mwA2A"><span id="mwA2E"><span id="mwA2I">[</span>118<span id="mwA2M">]</span></span></a></sup>

[Chandrika Kumaratunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandrika_Kumaratunga "Chandrika Kumaratunga"), who served as the former [president of Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Sri_Lanka "President of Sri Lanka") from 1994 to 2005 and former [Prime Minister of Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Sri_Lanka "Prime Minister of Sri Lanka") in 1994, is the daughter of [S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._W._R._D._Bandaranaike "S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike") and [Sirimavo Bandaranaike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirimavo_Bandaranaike "Sirimavo Bandaranaike"), who both served as [Prime Ministers of Ceylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Ceylon "Prime Minister of Ceylon") from 1956 to 1959, 1960 to 1965, 1970 to 1977 and 1994 to 2000. Her brother [Anura Bandaranaike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anura_Bandaranaike "Anura Bandaranaike") served as the [Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_Parliament_of_Sri_Lanka "Speaker of the Parliament of Sri Lanka") from 2000 to 2001

Also, former president Ranasinghe Premadasa's son Sajith Premadasa is the Opposition leader of Sri Lanka, who ran for the presidential election in 2019 as well.<sup about="#mwt394" id="cite_ref-119" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-119&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-119" id="mwA24"><span id="mwA28"><span id="mwA3A">[</span>119<span id="mwA3E">]</span></span></a></sup>

Also [Ranil Wickremesinghe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranil_Wickremesinghe "Ranil Wickremesinghe"), who served as prime minister of Sri Lanka from 1993 to 1994, 2001 to 2004, 2015 to 2018 and 2018 to 2019, is a nephew of former Sri Lankan president [J. R. Jayewardene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._R._Jayewardene "J. R. Jayewardene").<sup about="#mwt397" id="cite_ref-120" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-120&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-120" id="mwA3U"><span id="mwA3Y"><span id="mwA3c">[</span>120<span id="mwA3g">]</span></span></a></sup> Also, a defense state minister of his government, [Ruwan Wijewardene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruwan_Wijewardene "Ruwan Wijewardene"), is a cousin of [Ranil Wickremesinghe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranil_Wickremesinghe "Ranil Wickremesinghe").<sup about="#mwt400" id="cite_ref-121" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-121&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-121" id="mwA3s"><span id="mwA3w"><span id="mwA30">[</span>121<span id="mwA34">]</span></span></a></sup> Also, [Ruwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruwan_Wijewardene "Ruwan Wijewardene") is the great-grandson of UNP founder and Sri Lanka's first Prime Minister [D. S. Senanayake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._S._Senanayake "D. S. Senanayake"). [Ruwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruwan_Wijewardene "Ruwan Wijewardene") has been given a high priority in the party by [Ranil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranil_Wickremesinghe "Ranil Wickremesinghe"), by giving leadership roles.<sup about="#mwt403" id="cite_ref-122" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-122&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-122" id="mwA4M"><span id="mwA4Q"><span id="mwA4U">[</span>122<span id="mwA4Y">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt406" id="cite_ref-123" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-123&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-123" id="mwA4c"><span id="mwA4g"><span id="mwA4k">[</span>123<span id="mwA4o">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt409" id="cite_ref-124" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-124&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-124" id="mwA4s"><span id="mwA4w"><span id="mwA40">[</span>124<span id="mwA44">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism occurred in [Spanish Colonial America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_colonization_of_the_Americas "Spanish colonization of the Americas") when offices were given to family members.<sup about="#mwt412" id="cite_ref-125" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-125&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-125" id="mwA5I"><span id="mwA5M"><span id="mwA5Q">[</span>125<span id="mwA5U">]</span></span></a></sup>

[Juan Antonio Samaranch Salisachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Antonio_Samaranch_Salisachs "Juan Antonio Samaranch Salisachs"), son of [Juan Antonio Samaranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Antonio_Samaranch "Juan Antonio Samaranch") (president of the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) from 1980 to 2001), has been a member of the International Olympic Committee since 2001; his daughter, Maria Teresa Samaranch Salisachs, has been president of the Spanish Federation of Sports on Ice since 2005.<sup about="#mwt416" id="cite_ref-ElPais_126-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ElPais&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ElPais-126&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-ElPais-126" id="mwA5o"><span id="mwA5s"><span id="mwA5w">[</span>126<span id="mwA50">]</span></span></a></sup>

The [Marquess of Salisbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Gascoyne-Cecil,_3rd_Marquess_of_Salisbury "Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury"), who was [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom "Prime Minister of the United Kingdom") for three separate occasions from 1885 to 1902 for a total of approximately 14 years, appointed his nephew, [Arthur Balfour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Balfour "Arthur Balfour"), as [Chief Secretary for Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Secretary_for_Ireland "Chief Secretary for Ireland") in 1887 and later as prime minister in 1902. This is supposedly the origin of the phrase "[Bob's your uncle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob's_your_uncle "Bob's your uncle")".<sup about="#mwt419" id="cite_ref-127" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-127&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-127" id="mwA6U"><span id="mwA6Y"><span id="mwA6c">[</span>127<span id="mwA6g">]</span></span></a></sup>

In 1977, during his father-in-law [James Callaghan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Callaghan "James Callaghan")'s term as [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom "Prime Minister of the United Kingdom"), [Peter Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Jay_(diplomat) "Peter Jay (diplomat)") was appointed [ambassador to the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_Ambassador_to_the_United_States "United Kingdom Ambassador to the United States").<sup about="#mwt422" id="cite_ref-Guardian_obit_128-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Guardian obit&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Guardian_obit-128&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Guardian_obit-128" id="mwA64"><span id="mwA68"><span id="mwA7A">[</span>128<span id="mwA7E">]</span></span></a></sup> As Jay was just 40 years old, was not a diplomat and had never held any public office; the appointment caused some controversy and accusations of nepotism.<sup about="#mwt425" id="cite_ref-Observer_129-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Observer&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Observer-129&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-Observer-129" id="mwA7I"><span id="mwA7M"><span id="mwA7Q">[</span>129<span id="mwA7U">]</span></span></a></sup>

In February 2010, Sir Christopher Kelly, chairman of the [Committee on Standards in Public Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_Standards_in_Public_Life "Committee on Standards in Public Life"), said that more than 200 MPs used Parliamentary allowances to employ their own relatives in a variety of office roles. He suggested that the practice should be banned.<sup about="#mwt428" id="cite_ref-130" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-130&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-130" id="mwA7g"><span id="mwA7k"><span id="mwA7o">[</span>130<span id="mwA7s">]</span></span></a></sup>

North Yorkshire Police's Chief Constable [Grahame Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grahame_Maxwell?action=edit&redlink=1 "Grahame Maxwell (page does not exist)") was disciplined by the IPCC in 2011, but refused to resign, after admitting that he assisted a relative through the first stages of a recruitment process.<sup about="#mwt431" id="cite_ref-131" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-131&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-131" id="mwA74"><span id="mwA78"><span id="mwA8A">[</span>131<span id="mwA8E">]</span></span></a></sup>

Many Northern Irish politicians employ family members. In 2008, 19 elected politicians of the [Democratic Unionist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Unionist_Party "Democratic Unionist Party") (DUP) directly employed family members and relatives, comprising 27 of its 136 staff.<sup about="#mwt434" id="cite_ref-132" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-132&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-132" id="mwA8Q"><span id="mwA8U"><span id="mwA8Y">[</span>132<span id="mwA8c">]</span></span></a></sup>

In 2020, [Kate Bingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bingham "Kate Bingham"), the wife of [British Conservative Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") politician and then-[Financial Secretary to the Treasury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Secretary_to_the_Treasury "Financial Secretary to the Treasury") [Jesse Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Norman "Jesse Norman"), was appointed chair of the UK's Vaccine Taskforce—the group set up to lead UK efforts to find and manufacture a [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronavirus_disease_2019 "Coronavirus disease 2019") vaccine — despite other more qualified people being proposed.<sup about="#mwt437" id="cite_ref-133" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-133&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-133" id="mwA84"><span id="mwA88"><span id="mwA9A">[</span>133<span id="mwA9E">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism is found in the United States, though some employers and government agencies enact laws or policies intended to restrict the practice.

[Palm Beach County, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach_County,_Florida "Palm Beach County, Florida"), schools reinforced nepotism rules as of 2012 to ensure an "equitable work environment".<sup about="#mwt440" id="cite_ref-134" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-134&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-134" id="mwA9Y"><span id="mwA9c"><span id="mwA9g">[</span>134<span id="mwA9k">]</span></span></a></sup>

In December 2012, a report from _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ indicated various nepotism practices from the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia "District of Columbia") and Northern [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia")'s [Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Washington_Airports_Authority "Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority") (MWAA), including one family with five members working for the MWAA. One of the reasons given by the associate general counsel to defend the alleged nepotism was "if \[the employees are\] qualified and competed for \[the positions\] on their own, I don't see a problem with relatives working in the same organization."<sup about="#mwt443" id="cite_ref-135" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-135&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-135" id="mwA-A"><span id="mwA-E"><span id="mwA-I">[</span>135<span id="mwA-M">]</span></span></a></sup> The inspector general of the [U.S. Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_Transportation "U.S. Department of Transportation") and the US Congress pressured the MWAA to resolve practices of nepotism. Authority employees are no longer allowed to directly or indirectly influence the hiring or promotion of relatives, as documented in their ethics policy.<sup about="#mwt446" id="cite_ref-136" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-136&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-136" id="mwA-U"><span id="mwA-Y"><span id="mwA-c">[</span>136<span id="mwA-g">]</span></span></a></sup>

President [John Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Adams "John Adams") appointed his eldest son, [John Quincy Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams "John Quincy Adams"), as the first [United States Minister to Prussia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Germany "List of ambassadors of the United States to Germany").

Around 30 family members or relatives of President [Ulysses S. Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_S._Grant "Ulysses S. Grant") prospered financially in some way from either government appointments or employment.<sup about="#mwt449" id="cite_ref-137" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-137&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-137" id="mwA_A"><span id="mwA_E"><span id="mwA_I">[</span>137<span id="mwA_M">]</span></span></a></sup>

President Franklin Roosevelt submitted the name of his son [Elliott Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Roosevelt_(general) "Elliott Roosevelt (general)") to the Senate for promotion to brigadier general. Following threats of resignation and pressure, Elliott Roosevelt was made a rated pilot during World War II. A suitable vacancy could not be found for him after his father's death, and his last day of service was [VJ-Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VJ-Day "VJ-Day"). Franklin Roosevelt also appointed his eldest son, [James Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Roosevelt "James Roosevelt"), as an administrative assistant to the president and a secretary to the president. James Roosevelt was the White House coordinator for 18 federal agencies. _Time_ magazine suggested that he might be considered "Assistant President of the United States".

President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") made his brother-in-law, [Sargent Shriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sargent_Shriver "Sargent Shriver"), the first director of the [Peace Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Corps "Peace Corps") and his younger brother, [Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy "Robert F. Kennedy"), Attorney General.<sup about="#mwt452" id="cite_ref-138" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-138&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-138" id="mwA_4"><span id="mwA_8"><span id="mwBAA">[</span>138<span id="mwBAE">]</span></span></a></sup>

President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") faced lingering allegations stemming from the business dealings of his younger brother [Donald Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Nixon "Donald Nixon"), notably the younger Nixon's ties to the influential US defense businessman [Howard Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Hughes "Howard Hughes"), who loaned him $205,000 in 1956 to prop up his failing restaurant business; although the loan was never repaid, he subsequently maintained a close relationship to [John H. Meier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Meier "John H. Meier"), a prominent Hughes lieutenant.<sup about="#mwt455" id="cite_ref-139" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-139&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-139" id="mwBAc"><span id="mwBAg"><span id="mwBAk">[</span>139<span id="mwBAo">]</span></span></a></sup> Richard Nixon also appointed [John Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Eisenhower "John Eisenhower") as [United States Ambassador to Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Belgium "List of ambassadors of the United States to Belgium"). Richard Nixon was the father of Eisenhower's daughter-in-law, [Julie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Nixon_Eisenhower "Julie Nixon Eisenhower").

In 1979, [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), within weeks of being newly elected as Governor of Arkansas, appointed his wife, [Hillary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), to chair the Rural Health Advisory Committee.<sup about="#mwt458" id="cite_ref-140" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-140&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-140" id="mwBBE"><span id="mwBBI"><span id="mwBBM">[</span>140<span id="mwBBQ">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1993, newly elected as President of the United States, he again [appointed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton#Health_care_and_other_policy_initiatives "Hillary Clinton") his wife to chair a Task Force on National Health Care Reform. In 2013, Bill appointed his daughter, [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton "Chelsea Clinton"), a member of the governing board of the [Clinton Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Foundation "Clinton Foundation") and [Clinton Global Initiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Foundation#Clinton_Global_Initiative_(CGI)_and_CGI_U "Clinton Foundation").<sup about="#mwt461" id="cite_ref-141" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-141&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-141" id="mwBBk"><span id="mwBBo"><span id="mwBBs">[</span>141<span id="mwBBw">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trump_With_Family_February_1_2016.jpg)

The [Trump family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_family "Trump family")

In 2017, President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") was [accused of nepotism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiring_and_personnel_concerns_about_Donald_Trump#Family_members_in_major_roles "Hiring and personnel concerns about Donald Trump") after appointing both his son-in-law, [Jared Kushner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Kushner "Jared Kushner") and his older daughter [Ivanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivanka_Trump "Ivanka Trump") (married to Kushner) into [advisory roles to the president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Advisor_to_the_President_of_the_United_States "Senior Advisor to the President of the United States").<sup about="#mwt464" id="cite_ref-142" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-142&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-142" id="mwBCg"><span id="mwBCk"><span id="mwBCo">[</span>142<span id="mwBCs">]</span></span></a></sup> Neither Jared nor Ivanka had any experience in public service. In 2020, President Trump appointed Kyle Yunaska, the brother-in-law of his son [Eric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Trump "Eric Trump"), to the position of [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") Deputy Chief of Staff.

In 2024, President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") was accused of nepotism for pardoning his surviving son [Hunter Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Biden "Hunter Biden")'s federal felony gun and tax convictions, as well as any other offense against the United States occurring between January 1, 2014 and December 1, 2024.<sup about="#mwt467" id="cite_ref-143" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-143&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-143" id="mwBDE"><span id="mwBDI"><span id="mwBDM">[</span>143<span id="mwBDQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt470" id="cite_ref-144" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-144&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-144" id="mwBDU"><span id="mwBDY"><span id="mwBDc">[</span>144<span id="mwBDg">]</span></span></a></sup>

Current (since 1995)<sup about="#mwt473" id="cite_ref-145" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-145&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-145" id="mwBDs"><span id="mwBDw"><span id="mwBD0">[</span>145<span id="mwBD4">]</span></span></a></sup> US court rulings have held that the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") itself does not constitute an "agency" for the purposes of adhering to existing anti-nepotism laws on the books.<sup about="#mwt476" id="cite_ref-146" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-146&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-146" id="mwBEA"><span id="mwBEE"><span id="mwBEI">[</span>146<span id="mwBEM">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism is known to be practiced by the President of the Venezuelan National Assembly, [Cilia Flores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilia_Flores "Cilia Flores"). Nine positions in the National Assembly were filled by Flores' family members, including a mother-in-law, aunt, three siblings, a cousin and her mother, and two nephews.<sup about="#mwt479" id="cite_ref-147" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-147&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-147" id="mwBEc"><span id="mwBEg"><span id="mwBEk">[</span>147<span id="mwBEo">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt482" id="cite_ref-148" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-148&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-148" id="mwBEs"><span id="mwBEw"><span id="mwBE0">[</span>148<span id="mwBE4">]</span></span></a></sup>

The late [Robert Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mugabe "Robert Mugabe") was reported to be preparing his wife, [Grace Mugabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Mugabe "Grace Mugabe"), to be the next president of Zimbabwe while he was president.<sup about="#mwt486" id="cite_ref-149" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-149&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-149" id="mwBFM"><span id="mwBFQ"><span id="mwBFU">[</span>149<span id="mwBFY">]</span></span></a></sup>

Nepotism refers to partiality to family, whereas [cronyism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cronyism "Cronyism") refers to partiality to an associate or [friend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friend "Friend"). [Favoritism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-group_favoritism "In-group favoritism"), the broadest of the terms, refers to partiality based upon being part of a favored group, rather than job performance.<sup about="#mwt489" id="cite_ref-150" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-150&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism#cite_note-150" id="mwBFw"><span id="mwBF0"><span id="mwBF4">[</span>150<span id="mwBF8">]</span></span></a></sup>
